contenido: Canon 1 We have deemed it right that we also observe the rules set forth by the holy Fathers in each synod until now.

The holy and great and ecumenical synod, which by the grace of God and by the sanction of the most pious and faithful emperors Valentinian and Marcian Augustus has gathered in Chalcedon, metropolis of Bithynia, on the martyrdom of the most holy and victorious martyr Euphemia, has defined what follows.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, confirming the knowledge of the faith of the disciples, said: "My peace I give to you, my peace I leave with you," so that no one would differ from his neighbor in the dogmas of piety, but that the preaching of the truth would be announced to all equally.

Therefore, this holy and great and ecumenical synod, rejecting the present heresy that has recently arisen against it, and expelling from the right faith those who, now by confusion, now by division, strive to annul the mystery of the one and the same Lord our Jesus Christ, and on the contrary confirming the dogmas of those who persevere in the truth of the faith, preaches one and the same Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, the same perfect in deity and the same perfect in humanity, the same God true and true man, of rational soul and body, consubstantial with the Father according to the deity, and the same consubstantial with us according to humanity, similar to us in everything except sin; begotten of the Father before the ages according to the deity, and in the last days the same, for us and for our salvation, of Mary the Virgin Mother of God according to humanity; to one and the same Christ the Son, the only begotten Lord, who is to be recognized in two natures without confusion, without change, without division, without separation; without the difference of natures being in any way suppressed because of the union, but rather, the property of both natures is saved, and they are concurrent in a single person and subsistence; not divided nor divided into two persons, but one and the same only begotten Son God the Word Lord Jesus Christ: as from the beginning the prophets concerning him, and Jesus Christ himself taught us, and the symbol of the Fathers has handed down to us.

Having therefore defined and composed these things with all diligence and care from all sides, the holy and ecumenical synod sanctioned that it is lawful for no one to utter, or write, or compose, or feel, or otherwise teach another faith. Those who dare to compose another faith, or proclaim it, or teach it, or give another symbol to those who want to convert to the knowledge of the truth from gentility, or from Judaism, or from any heresy: these, if they are bishops or clerics, let the bishops be alien to the episcopate and the clerics to the clergy; and whether monks or laymen, let them be anathematized.

Canon 6 Absolutely no one should be ordained, neither a priest, nor a deacon, nor in general any of those who are in the ecclesiastical order, unless the one who is ordained is preached especially in the Church of the city, or of the possession, or of martyrdom, or of the monastery. And those who are ordained at all, the holy synod decreed that such laying on of hands be void, and that they may nowhere minister, to the reproach of him who ordained them.

Canon 7 To those who have once been counted in the clergy, or to the monks, we decree that they go neither to the military nor to secular dignity. Or, doing so and not repenting to return to what they first chose for God, be anathematized.

Canon 8 Let the clerics of the xenodochi of the poor and of the monasteries and of the martyrs remain under the power of the bishops who are in each city, according to the tradition of the holy Fathers, and do not depart due to contumacy from their bishop. Those who dare in any way to subvert the constitutions and not be subject to their bishop, if they are clerics, are subject to canonical corrections; and whether monks or laymen, they are separated from communion.

Canon 9 If a clergyman has a matter against a clergyman, he must not leave his own bishop and do not resort to secular trials: but let him first discuss the matter before his own bishop, or certainly, with the consent of the same bishop, the judgment of the dispute be made before whom both wish. If anyone does anything other than this, let him be subject to canonical corrections. If a clergyman has a dispute against his own bishop, or also against another bishop: he must be judged before the synod of the province. If a bishop or clergyman has a dispute against the metropolitan of the same province: go, either to the exarch of the diocese, or to the seat of the royal Constantinople, and be judged before him.

Canon 10 It is not lawful for a clergyman to be counted in the canon, according to time, in the Churches of two cities: namely, in that in which he was ordained from the beginning, and in that to which he was transferred as for a reason of greater esteem: those who do this should be restored to their own Church, in which from the beginning they were ordained, and only there minister. If someone has already been transferred from one Church to another, nothing that belongs to the previous Church, whether of martyrs, of xenodochios, or of ptochiotrophs, participates. And those who dare, after the definition of the great and ecumenical synod, to do something that is prohibited, the holy synod decreed that they be deposed from their own degree.

Canon 11 We decree that all the poor and those who need help, with examination, travel through the provinces with ecclesiastical letters, that is, peaceful ones: not, however, with commendatory letters, since commendatory letters are given only to the most honorable people.

Canon 12 It has come to our attention that some, resorting to the powers against the ecclesiastical constitutions, have, out of pragmatism, divided a province into two, so that for this reason there are two metropolitans in the same province. The holy synod has therefore decreed that from now on nothing similar should be attempted by a bishop. He who tries it, let him fall from his own degree. The cities that by imperial letters have been honored with the metropolitan name, enjoy only the honor, and the bishop who administers his Church: except, of course, the rights of the true metropolis.
Canon 13 Pilgrim clerics and anagnosts must not minister anywhere in another city without letters of commendation from their bishop.

Canon 14 Since in some provinces it has been granted to readers and singers to take wives: the holy synod decreed that it is not lawful for any of them to take a foreign wife. And those who have already engendered children from such nuptials, if they went ahead to circumcise them among the heretics, offer them to the communion of the Catholic Church; and they cannot henceforth join heretics. If anyone does anything other than this, let him be subject to canonical corrections.

Canon 15 Let no deaconess be ordained before the fortieth year, and this with diligent examination. If, after having received the laying on of hands and having remained for some time in the ministry, she gives herself over to the nuptials, making an affront to the grace of God: she, together with him who joined her, let her be anathematized.

Canon 16 It is not lawful for a virgin who dedicated herself to the Lord God, and also for monks, to unite in nuptials. If anyone is found doing this, they are excommunicated. We decree, however, that the local bishop have the authority to use humanity toward them.

Canon 17 Rural or village parishes remain unaltered in each Church together with the bishops who have them, and especially if they have administered them for a period of thirty years, having them without commotion. If within thirty years there has been, or will be, a controversy regarding these: it may be lawful for those who say they have been injured to promote them before the provincial synod. If anyone is injured by his metropolitan, let him be judged before the exarch of the diocese or before the Constantinopolitan see, as has been said. If a city has been built or will be built again by imperial power: the order of civil and public forms also follows that of ecclesiastical parishes.

Canon 18 The crime of conspiracy or faction is completely prohibited also by external laws: much more must this be prohibited from being done in the Church of God. If, then, some clergymen or monks are found conspiring, or conspiring, or lying in wait for bishops or clerics: let them fall completely from their own rank.

Canon 19 It has come to our attention that synods of bishops are not held in the provinces, and for this reason many ecclesiastical things that need correction are neglected. Therefore, the holy synod has decreed that, according to the canons of the holy Fathers, twice a year the bishops should meet, one for each province, where the metropolitan approves, and correct whatever has arisen. And the bishops who do not meet, remaining in their cities, and this in good health and free from all necessary and unavoidable occupation, be corrected fraternally.

Canon 20 For clerics who minister in a Church, as we have already defined, it is not licit to be ordained in the Church of another city, but rather to remain in the one in which from the beginning they deserved to minister, with the exception of those who, losing their own homeland, out of necessity emigrated to another Church. If any bishop, after this definition, receives a cleric belonging to another bishop: both the one who was received and the one who received are excommunicated, until the clergyman who emigrated returns to his own Church.
Canon 21 Clerics or laymen who accuse bishops or clerics are not to be admitted to the accusation simply and without examination, unless their reputation has first been explored.

Canon 22 It is not lawful for clerics, after the death of their bishop, to plunder the things that belong to him, as is already prohibited by the ancient canons. Those who attempt to do this will be in danger as to their own grades.

Canon 23 It has come to the ears of the holy synod that some clerics and monks, not having any commission from their own bishop, and sometimes also excommunicated by him, coming to the royal city of Constantinople and staying for a long time there, make riots and disturb the ecclesiastical state and confuse the houses of some. The holy synod has therefore decreed that such should first be admonished by the defender of the most holy Church of Constantinople to leave the royal city. If they shamelessly persevere in the same thing, let them be expelled by the same defender, even against their will, and return to their own places.

Canon 24 Monasteries that have once been consecrated by the decree of the bishop remain monasteries forever, and the things that belong to them are kept for the monastery, and they cannot henceforth be made into secular habitations. Those who allow this to be done are subject to canonical corrections.

Canon 25 Since some metropolitans, as we have heard, neglect the flocks entrusted to them and postpone the ordinations of bishops: it has seemed to the holy synod that the ordinations of bishops should be carried out within three months, unless an unavoidable necessity prolongs the time of delay. If anyone does not observe these things, let him be subject to canonical corrections. And the income of the widowed Church be kept in full in the power of the treasurer of the same Church.

Canon 26 Since in some Churches, as we have heard, bishops deal with ecclesiastical things without treasurers: it has seemed that every Church that has a bishop also has a treasurer of its own clergy, who according to the opinion of its bishop dispenses ecclesiastical things: so that the administration of the Church is not without witnesses, and for this reason its faculties are dispersed and a curse is attributed to the priesthood. If anyone does not do this, let him be subject to the divine canonical constitutions.

Canon 27 To those who kidnap women under the name of marriage, or cooperate, or consent to the kidnappers: the holy synod commanded that, if they were clerics, they should fall from their own rank; and if laymen, let them be anathematized.

Canon 28 Following everywhere the definitions of the holy Fathers, and knowing the canons that have now been recited, we also define and sanction the same things regarding the privileges of the most holy Church of Constantinople, the new Rome. For to the throne of ancient Rome, because of the empire of that city, the Fathers rightly attributed privileges; and with the same consideration, the one hundred and fifty most loving bishops of God attributed equal privileges to the most holy throne of the new Rome, rightly judging that the city that has been honored with the empire and the senate, and enjoys equal privileges with the ancient royal Rome, also in ecclesiastical things should be magnified like that, existing in second place after it; and that only the metropolitans of the dioceses of Pontus and of Asia and of Thrace, and furthermore also those who among the barbarian nations are bishops of the said dioceses, be ordained by the said most holy throne of the most holy Church of Constantinople: namely, by ordaining the metropolitan of each of the said dioceses, with the provincial bishops, to the bishops of the province, as is commanded by the divine canons; and that the metropolitans of the said dioceses be ordained, as has been said, by the archbishop of Constantinople, with convenient elections made according to custom and referred to him.

Canon 29 Reducing a bishop to the degree of presbyterate is sacrilege. If for some just cause he is removed from the episcopal act, he should not have the place of the priesthood either. If without any crime he is removed from the dignity, he be restored to the episcopal dignity.

Canon 30 Since the most reverend bishops of the Egyptians have hereby deferred to subscribe to the volume of Leo, most holy archbishop of ancient Rome, not as repugnant to the Catholic faith, but saying that it is customary in the Egyptian diocese not to do anything similar without the opinion and decree of the archbishop; and that is why they ask for a delay until the ordination of the future archbishop of the great city of the Alexandrians: we have considered it reasonable and humane that they be given a delay, remaining in their own capacity in the royal city, until the archbishop of the great city of the Alexandrians is ordained. Therefore, having them detained or giving security, if possible, or being bound by an oath, only then do they leave.
